pronunciation.notes: **None** rhymes with **one** and **fun**, not with **bone** or **gone**, even though the spelling looks similar to **bone**.

senses.definition: not any person or thing in a group, or not any amount of something
senses.explanation: **None** is usually followed by **of**: *none of the students*, *none of the money*. It stands alone when the group it refers to is already clear from what was just said.

examples.text: None of the students passed the exam.
I asked everyone for help, but none came.
None of this makes any sense to me.
Of the three plans, none was approved.

compare.note: **no** goes directly before a noun (*no money*); **none** stands alone or is followed by **of** (*none of the money*)
**nothing** refers to no thing at all, with no group in mind; **none** picks out not any member of a stated or implied group

adaptation.semantic: **None** covers both no person or thing in a countable group (*none of the students*) and no amount of something uncountable (*none of the money*); many languages use two different words for these, or none for a pronoun at all and instead negate the verb.
adaptation.grammar: With a plural noun, **none** can take a singular verb in careful writing (*none of them is ready*) or a plural verb in everyday speech (*none of them are ready*); many languages have no such choice.

phrases.definition: not at all, or only just

examples.text: The hotel room was none too clean.
We arrived none too soon; the train was already leaving.

phrases.definition: knowing no more than before, despite an explanation or an event

examples.text: I read the instructions twice and was still none the wiser.
She explained the rule again, but I was none the wiser.

usage_note: Formal writing often treats **none** as singular even with a plural noun (*none of them is ready*), but everyday speech usually treats it as plural (*none of them are ready*); both are acceptable.

learner_errors.incorrect: None people came to the party.
learner_errors.correct: No one came to the party.
learner_errors.note: **None** does not go directly before a noun; use **no** before a noun, or **none of** before a noun with **the**, a possessive, or a pronoun.

learner_errors.incorrect: None of the water were clean.
learner_errors.correct: None of the water was clean.
learner_errors.note: With an uncountable noun, **none** always takes a singular verb.
